units: kit units: 1 = one road tile (the game scales a tile to 8 m). +Y up. All pieces have their origin at ground level (y=0), centred on their footprint; top-level node transform is identity.

conventions.rotation: three.js rotation.y = +PI/2 (counter-clockwise seen from above) maps N->W, W->S, S->E, E->N (and a -Z front becomes -X). rotation.y = PI: N<->S, E<->W.
conventions.buildingFront: Every Kenney city building (commercial, suburban, industrial) has its shop-front / front door on -Z (N); most also have a small back door on +Z. Restaurants/landmarks in restaurants.glb face +Z (S).
conventions.footprint: footprintTiles = [tiles along X, tiles along Z]; origin "tile-center" for odd x odd footprints, "tile-corner" for even x even, "edge-mid" for mixed - i.e. pieces are always centred on their footprint.
conventions.roadOpenings: opens = edges (in the default rotation) where asphalt (>=0.3 wide) reaches the edge of the piece. openings[] gives each one exactly: side, at (local x,z of the middle of the opening on that edge), span (asphalt extent along the edge, local coordinate), y (road surface height there), aligned (edge lies on the tile grid and span == a tile centre +-0.4, i.e. it mates with a standard road-straight). driveways[] = narrow asphalt cuts through the sidewalk (0.26 wide). edges{} lists every surface run along each edge (road / sidewalk / paving / other / none=no geometry).

roadGeometry.note: Measured from road-straight (runs along X). Coordinates across the road (z) in kit units; x8 for metres.
roadGeometry.edgeStrip: darker asphalt strips (gutter / parking strip) at 0.3 <= |z| <= 0.4 (0.1 wide), same height as the lanes

centreLine.style: continuous on road-straight; uses the marking swatch

roadGeometry.suggestedDrivingLineOffset: z = +-0.155 lane centres (or +-0.2 to use the full lane + edge strip). Right-hand traffic: travelling +X drive at z=+0.155 (the vehicle's right is +Z), travelling -X at z=-0.155.

curb.note: vertical step from asphalt (y=0.01) to sidewalk (y=0.02) at |z|=0.4

construction-barrier.note: guard-rail overlay; place on top of construction with the same transform

road-bend.note: tight 90° bend (radius 0.5 to the centre line, around the S-W corner); NE corner beyond the outer sidewalk is EMPTY (no ground) - put a ground tile under it or use road-bend-sidewalk

road-bend-barrier.note: guard-rail overlay; place on top of road-bend with the same transform

kit-commercial.glb.notes: detail-awning(-wide) / detail-overhang(-wide): the high/back edge (z=+0.248 / +0.25) goes against a wall, the canopy and posts stick out toward -Z (i.e. they belong on a -Z building front, translated so their +Z edge touches the wall).

kit-industrial.glb.notes: windmill / windmill-low keep a child node "blades" with its pivot at the hub (spin about local X).

kit-cars.glb.notes: Vehicles face +Z (front wheels at +Z), origin on the ground under the body centre. Car-kit scale: a sedan is ~2.6 units long, so scale cars down relative to road tiles (DOCS.md uses x1.5 on a metre scale). Children: body (+ optional door/doors/arm/grill/spoiler/wheel-back/trash) and wheel-front-left, wheel-front-right, wheel-back-left, wheel-back-right with their pivot at the wheel centre - spin about local X.

restaurants.glb.notes: Landmarks face +Z (door/shop-front toward the street on +Z), lot 0.96 x 0.96 with a paved pad (y 0..0.012) and a small terrace between the facade (z ~ +0.15..0.19) and the lot edge. Materials per landmark: brand (main brand colour), awning (awning stripes / canopy), props (shared 64x64 palette texture for all untinted colours), food (Kenney food colormap, only where a Kenney food item is used). The child node <name>-sign is the giant rooftop food / sign with its pivot at its base centre (spin about Y: rest-doner spit; bob/rotate the others). Node extras (three.js userData): title, brandColor, awningColor, door [x,y,z] (pickup point), counter (serving hatch, doner/icecream).
